_: V90BitsToSymbol's constructor owns a V90Mapper and a symbol buffer and
writes five scalars; two more fields at +0x14 and +0x18 it deliberately
leaves alone.  The mutations below split into three groups: the ones a
whole-object comparison over never-zeroed storage catches, the ones the
allocation accounting catches, and the ones only the free/free_null
split catches.  A mutation that makes the destructor dereference null
is caught by the run dying, which is still a failing run.

_: V90BitsToSymbol::process(unsigned char *, unsigned int), the FILL, and it
is driven by t_v90modchain and not by t_v90btsproc: its live arm calls
mapper->process on its first statement, so it needs a real constructed
V90Mapper behind the pointer rather than the invented address that
binary installs.
FOUR ANCHORS REACH BACK TO THE SIGNATURE.  The SIZE_NOT_SET arm and the
pending-flag tail are written out VERBATIM in both overloads -- one
status alphabet, one message -- so a find taken from inside either run
matches twice and is rejected.  The five anchors in v90btsproc.json that
quoted those lines were extended for the same reason when this function
landed.
NOT HERE: turning `if (extraSymbolsPending) extraSymbolsPending = 0;`
into an unconditional store.  It writes the same byte on every input the
flag can hold and no test can separate the two; what holds the object's
spelling is the `cmpb $0x0,0x20(%ebx) ; je` at 0x2fcb6.  Finding F7430.
